items.analysis: Military actions in the Strait of Hormuz have continued alongside diplomatic maneuvering, with U.S. A-10 aircraft destroying Iranian speedboats and CENTCOM reporting the interception of multiple Iranian attack drones targeting commercial vessels. President Trump announced a deal would be signed on June 14, stating the strait would open immediately with no fees or Iranian control, yet Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi has repeatedly asserted joint Iranian-Omani sovereignty, service fees, and separate rules for military vessels. The Institute for the Study of War highlighted that the phased MoU sequence gives Iran economic relief before nuclear talks, a structure that may reduce U.S. leverage, while Iranian media frame it as a tactical pause. Vessel traffic data from the past 24 hours show no ships using the Iranian traffic separation scheme, with only a few transiting through Omani waters along the Project Freedom safe route, underscoring the commercial sector’s persistent avoidance of zones subject to Iranian claims. This alignment of Iranian media, IRGC outlets, and senior diplomacy around maximalist demands, contrasted with the U.S. stance of no Iranian management, complicates the path from the expected MoU to a durable settlement.

items.description: Axios reported that the U.S. and Iran are expected to sign a deal on Sunday extending a ceasefire by 60 days, reopening the Strait of Hormuz, and beginning nuclear talks, with Pakistan and Qatar mediating and a virtual signing planned.
items.rawSummary: The U.S.-Iran diplomatic process remains at a critical juncture with an electronic signing ceremony scheduled for June 14, though Tehran denies a deal is finalized and President Trump warns of an 'ultimate alternative'; separately, a GAO report highlights severe readiness shortfalls in the U.S. F-35 fleet.
items.analysis: The diplomatic push for a U.S.-Iran agreement remains volatile. Pakistani and Saudi foreign ministers confirmed an electronic signing ceremony for June 14, and Axios reported a deal would extend a ceasefire by 60 days, reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and launch nuclear talks, but Iran's Fars news agency cited officials denying a finalized deal and calling Sunday a test of negotiator resolve. President Trump then posted on Truth Social that the deal will be signed tomorrow and threatened an unspecified 'ultimate alternative' if it does not, directly contradicting Tehran's stance. A senior Israeli official told N12 the terms are a 'shit deal,' underscoring deep skepticism in Jerusalem. U.S. officials have publicly demanded Iran destroy its nuclear materials, dismantle its program, and halt proxy funding before any sanctions relief, while military planners have quietly discussed deploying specialists to secure enriched uranium if a deal is reached. Meanwhile, a new Government Accountability Office report found that only 44% of U.S. F-35 jets are mission capable and just 25% can perform their full range of missions, requiring an additional $13.7 billion in sustainment costs through 2031 and highlighting readiness challenges even as military contingencies are considered.

items.title: Islamabad, Pakistan: Trump reposted Prime Minister Sharif's statement reaffirming the 24-hour signing timeline, signaling continued U.S. optimism for the deal.
items.description: Trump reposted Prime Minister Sharif's statement reaffirming the 24-hour signing timeline, signaling continued U.S. optimism for the deal.
items.rawSummary: Pakistan's Prime Minister reiterated a 24-hour timeline for signing the U.S.-Iran peace deal and Trump reposted his message, even as Iran stated it would not be signed the next day, leaving the finalization schedule uncertain.
items.analysis: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced earlier in the day that the U.S.-Iran peace deal will be signed within 24 hours, with Pakistan preparing an electronic signing immediately after and technical-level talks to follow next week. Hours later, Iran stated that the agreement would not be signed tomorrow but could be finalized in the coming days, introducing some uncertainty around the immediate timeline. Later, Sharif repeated the 24-hour deadline and Trump reposted Sharif's message, signaling continued alignment between Washington and Islamabad on the expedited schedule. The final agreed text was reached on June 12, and the rapid diplomatic progress has drawn expressions of support from Qatar and Saudi Arabia. Vice President JD Vance emphasized that no funds will be released until Iran fully complies, including complete dismantlement of its nuclear program and removal of all nuclear material, while Israeli Defense Minister Katz ordered the IDF to prepare for independent action. Islamabad remains the central venue for a process that could reshape regional economic and security dynamics, though conditions and opposition from key U.S. and Israeli figures continue to mark the path toward finalization.

items.title: Paris, France, France: President Macron stated that France is the only country in Europe with a large language model capable of competing with the US and China, citing Mistral AI.
items.description: President Macron stated that France is the only country in Europe with a large language model capable of competing with the US and China, citing Mistral AI.
items.rawSummary: President Macron touted France's large language model capabilities via Mistral AI as the only European peer of US and Chinese systems, while Franco-German defense cooperation continues to unravel and France pursues war crimes investigations and sanctions against Israeli officials.
items.analysis: President Macron stated it is time to resume dialogue with Russia, insisting Europeans must be at the peace table for their own security architecture. The Franco-German defense relationship continues to unravel: after the FCAS next-generation fighter program was declared dead and France dropped out of the Eurodrone project, the MGCS tank project now faces a possible French exit. Rheinmetall's CEO said France is considering slashing its budget to less than half, with only €25 million paid out since 2017, Reuters reported, marking the third major joint defense initiative to founder alongside the stalled FCAS and scrapped Eurodrone. In parallel, France opened a war crimes and torture investigation into Israel's treatment of French activists detained in May, and in coordination with Britain, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, and Norway, imposed sanctions and entry bans on Finance Minister Smotrich, four settler leaders, and 21 violent settlers, mirroring an earlier ban on National Security Minister Ben-Gvir. This diplomatic drive occurred amid a row after Israel's Ambassador declared a preference for 'anyone rather than Mélenchon' for the presidency and revealed meetings with far-right figures, prompting demands he be summoned. Domestically, prediction market Polymarket showed Jordan Bardella as the most likely presidential winner at 27 percent, reflecting a broad shift away from the centre. France also announced its suspicion that Israeli firm BlackCore ran online influence operations targeting French local elections and elections in New York and Scotland, as well as activities in Angola and Togo; investigators have not identified who commissioned the campaigns, and France has asked Israel for help in the investigation. Meanwhile, President Macron highlighted France's artificial intelligence ambitions, stating it is the only European country with a large language model capable of competing with US and Chinese peers, citing Mistral AI.

items.description: Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis warned that China's 30% share of global manufacturing capacity could destroy industries across Europe and urged the issue to be taken seriously.
items.rawSummary: China confronts diplomatic tensions with Japan and the United States while facing a warning from Greece over its dominant manufacturing capacity, as its central bank extends a record gold-buying streak.
items.analysis: China has accused Japan of rapid military expansionism, likening its actions to pre-World War II militarism, and its Commerce Ministry condemned the United States for weaponizing national security to suppress Chinese growth after more firms were designated as 'military companies.' Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis separately warned that China's 30% share of global manufacturing capacity threatens to destroy industries across Europe, underscoring mounting international unease over Beijing's economic power. The People's Bank of China deepened its economic buffers by purchasing more than 10 tonnes of gold in May, its largest monthly addition since January 2025, bringing official reserves to a record 2,331 tonnes amid a 19-month buying streak.

items.title: Nearby Iranian positions (implied operational area), Iran: U.S. Central Command announced that U.S. forces redirected 141 vessels and disabled 9 more in support of the naval blockade of Iran, while 42 ships have been allowed to pass with humanitarian cargo.
items.description: U.S. Central Command announced that U.S. forces redirected 141 vessels and disabled 9 more in support of the naval blockade of Iran, while 42 ships have been allowed to pass with humanitarian cargo.
items.rawSummary: Iran has begun collapsing tunnels and rigging mines to protect its near weapons-grade uranium, while U.S. forces enforce a naval blockade that has redirected 141 vessels and disabled 9 more, amid ongoing diplomatic uncertainty following Trump's declaration that the war ended.
items.analysis: Following CENTCOM’s framing of U.S. strikes through June 10 as self-defense, President Trump escalated by threatening nightly attacks and the seizure of Kharg Island and oil infrastructure, then suddenly announced on June 11 that the war had ended and Iran had settled without clear terms. A detailed assessment indicated Iran is using information operations, including claiming the Strait of Hormuz closed, to pressure the U.S. into a deal and treating the conflict as war rather than negotiations. In a Bloomberg interview, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei acknowledged that a February U.S. missile strike killing over 150 people at a girls’ school in Iran was ‘really terrible,’ while noting that a human made the final call rather than the AI model. Iranian state media Mehr News publicized a 14‑point draft memorandum that includes a permanent ceasefire and a $300 billion reconstruction fund, though the U.S. denied the proposal and the draft still requires Iranian authority review. CBS reported that U.S. officials are discussing contingency plans involving the Department of Energy’s Nuclear Emergency Support Team to retrieve Iranian nuclear material. Five U.S. intelligence sources told CNN that Iran has begun collapsing tunnels and rigging entrances with explosive mines to secure its roughly half‑ton cache of near weapons‑grade uranium, making the stockpile much harder and more dangerous to access. At the same time, U.S. Central Command reported that its naval blockade of Iran had redirected 141 vessels and disabled 9, while allowing 42 ships with humanitarian cargo to pass.

items.title: Iranian regime governmental centers (unspecified locations), Iran: Tehran warned that Israel's strike on Beirut could derail negotiations with Washington.
items.description: Tehran warned that Israel's strike on Beirut could derail negotiations with Washington.
items.rawSummary: Negotiations over a potential U.S.-Iran framework agreement have stalled, with a senior Iranian advisor stating there will be no more talks for now and Tehran warning that Israel's Beirut strike could derail the diplomatic track, while hardline domestic criticism persists and conflicting accounts of the proposed terms remain.
items.analysis: Negotiations over a U.S.-Iran framework agreement appear to have stalled, with an advisor to the Iranian negotiating team stating there will be no more talks for now, despite Qatari mediators having arrived in Tehran earlier to help finalize a deal. Tehran also warned that Israel's recent strike on Beirut could derail the diplomatic process. Earlier, Foreign Minister Araghchi’s readout suggested a possible elite consensus, but hardline domestic opposition remains fierce, notably from Deputy Parliament Chairman Nabavian who criticized the deal as giving the U.S. control over reconstruction spending and preventing rebuilding of Iran's nuclear program. Conflicting official accounts of the proposed terms—with a U.S. official describing no cash transfers and a limited 60-day oil sales window, while an Iranian official described $25 billion in unfrozen assets and full sanctions relief after 60 days—continued to fuel confusion over the deal's actual framework. Separately, authorities confirmed a limited cyberattack on four banks without compromising customer data, state media announced arrangements for Supreme Leader Khamenei's funeral, and Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf condemned Israeli violations in southern Lebanon, underscoring persistent regional security tensions.

Separately, authorities confirmed a limited cyberattack on four banks without compromising customer data, state media announced arrangements for Supreme Leader Khamenei's funeral, and Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf condemned Israeli violations in southern Lebanon, underscoring persistent regional security tensions.
